scenes.interruption: Scroll callbacks update the visible properties directly; a new gesture owns the header state immediately.
scenes.accessibility: The condensed masthead and content remain readable with reduced motion.
scenes.performance: Update only derived scalar state and transform/opacity properties in the scroll callback.

scenes.interruption: Pointer down cancels snapping, current pixel offset becomes the drag origin, and release snaps to the nearest index.
scenes.accessibility: Every segment is a button, so gesture navigation is not required.
scenes.performance: Use one native swipe container and one translate-based indicator.

scenes.interruption: A new tap cancels active effects and restarts from the settled button frame; counters update even when motion is disabled.
scenes.accessibility: A motion toggle disables particles and burst animation without blocking the reaction count.
scenes.performance: Use lightweight declarative nodes for the sample; move to Canvas when particle count grows substantially.

evidence.comparison: analysis comparison JSON generated by scripts/analyze_motion_trace.py compare

notes: Scroll-linked motion uses onDidScroll in ArkUI rather than a timer.
Swipe tabs map to Swiper plus a custom animated indicator.
Reaction burst maps the button sequence to keyframeAnimateTo and secondary effects to delayed property animations.
